summary: Shipped three more built-in Modbus device profiles for the solar hardware installers actually buy outside the SolarEdge/SMA/Fronius/Huawei world: sungrow-sh-hybrid (Sungrow SH residential hybrids -- #2 in global inverter shipments), deye-hybrid (one map covering Deye, Sunsynk, and Sol-Ark rebadges), and eastron-sdm630-meter (a read-only 3-phase meter). Sungrow and Deye also pre-declare Modbus commands (ems_mode/batt_force/batt_force_power/export_limit/export_limit_enable/batt_min_soc/batt_max_soc for Sungrow; work_mode/solar_sell/grid_charge/max_sell_power for Deye) -- the first built-in profiles to do so -- though every command stays inert until an admin turns on the device's actuation AND bench-verifies the register, since sign/scale/units differ by firmware. This required two additions to the Modbus register-map driver (infra/iot/modbus/regmap.go): an optional inputReader interface + Point.Input so a map can bind INPUT registers (Modbus fn 4) alongside the existing holding-register (fn 3) path -- clusters now partition by bank first, since the two function codes can never share a round trip -- and a new PF32 PType decoding IEEE-754 float32 (the encoding cheap meters like the Eastron use). entities.TelemetryKey gained a matching RegInput field and "f32" became a valid RegKind, threaded through the profile CRUD/import-export/builtin-seed paths and the frontend profile editor (a new "Input register (fn 4)" toggle per telemetry key). Five new built-in Flow Engine templates ship alongside these on the $inverter slot: solar-self-consumption and solar-self-sufficiency (derived series persisted for charts/rollups), solar-battery-guard (low-SoC alert + a guarded force-charge command below a critical floor), solar-export-limit (caps grid export via a guarded command -- the control showcase), and solar-inverter-health (overheat + abnormal-running-state alerts). Finally, a new in-app knowledge base (apps/myiotsan/kb, served at GET /api/kb and GET /api/kb/{slug}, readable by viewer and operator as well as admin) ships eight compiled-in Markdown setup articles covering every new profile, the SunSpec-native path, Modbus TCP vs RTU-over-TCP, an RS485-to-TCP gateway how-to, and how to verify a control register before enabling actuation -- surfaced in the frontend as a new Help page with a dependency-free Markdown renderer. Live-boot verified: the knowledge base is served, all profiles and flow templates seed correctly, and the FC04/float32/word-swap read path decodes correctly against a Modbus mock.
compatibility: Fully additive and backward-compatible for every existing install. Point.Input defaults false, so every existing register map and Reader (including the SunSpec decoder and the huawei-sun2000 profile) is read exactly as before over holding registers only; a Reader that does not implement the new optional inputReader interface only errors if a map is deliberately configured to bind an input-register point, rather than silently misreading. The three new profiles and five new flow templates are additive rows seeded alongside the existing catalog (present-by-slug is skipped, so a site's own edits to a same-named profile/flow are never overwritten). Every command the two new actuating profiles declare ships with the device's actuationEnabled left off by default (the same posture every other command-capable profile in this app has always shipped with), so no existing or newly-adopted device can be written to until an admin deliberately opts it in and bench-verifies the register for their specific model/firmware. The knowledge base is read-only reference content compiled into the binary (go:embed) -- it needs no network access and adds no new attack surface beyond the two new GET-only routes, which the RBAC catalog explicitly grants to viewer/operator, matching the read posture of the device/profile catalog it documents. New frontend i18n strings (nav.help, kb.subtitle, kb.empty, profiles.regInput*) are translated across all four locales -- en/ms/zh/ar.
